metadata.description: Practical made-up price-buddy estimates for a wine list: base market price and Michelin-star restaurant list price in EUR per 750ml bottle.

assumptions.bottle_size: 750ml unless original item is sake/fortified/non-standard; still normalized as a listed bottle price
assumptions.base_price: plausible normal retail/market estimate, not guaranteed current availability
assumptions.michelin_star_price: plausible 1-star to 3-star restaurant wine-list price using tiered markup; trophy wines use lower multiple, affordable wines higher multiple
assumptions.fictional_items: assigned fantasy prices so the list remains complete

wines.name: Albariño Do Ferreiro Cepas Vellas 2019
wines.notes: Premium Albariño from old vines; priced above standard Rías Baixas bottlings but below top-tier white Burgundy equivalents. Estimate reflects a serious retail bottle and a typical Michelin-star list markup for a high-demand, food-friendly white wine.
wines.tasting_note: A serious Albariño likely to show citrus peel, white peach, green apple and blossom, with a subtle herbal edge and a touch of leesy breadth. The palate should be taut yet layered, combining brisk acidity with a fine, slightly waxy texture and a dry, savoury finish that leans toward sea spray and crushed stone rather than overt fruit.

wines.name: Albariño Pazo Barrantes 2020
wines.notes: Premium Rías Baixas Albariño from a well-regarded producer; priced as a serious restaurant-list estimate rather than a live-verified retail quote. Suitable for a polished by-the-glass or premium bottle placement in a Michelin-star setting.
wines.tasting_note: A poised Albariño likely to show ripe citrus, white peach and pear, with subtle floral and fennel notes over a clean, stony frame. Expect a supple but focused palate, brisk acidity and a lightly textured mid-palate, finishing dry, savoury and neatly saline rather than overtly exuberant.

Expect a dry, medium-light palate with brisk acidity, a fine textural grip, and a clean, mouth-watering finish that should make it especially versatile at the table.

wines.name: Albariño Pazo Señorans Selección de Añada 2015

The palate should be medium-bodied and textural, with bright but integrated acidity, a gentle saline edge and a dry, savoury finish that balances fruit depth with quiet complexity.

wines.name: Cahors Château du Cèdre 2017

Yves Cuilleron’s Les Vignes d’à Côté is a Rhône Viognier with solid mid-tier restaurant positioning: ripe but not extravagant, usually priced above entry-level regional whites yet below the domaine’s more serious single-site wines. Estimate reflects a practical retail-to-restaurant translation for a 2019 bottle in good condition.
wines.tasting_note: A poised, Rhône-style Viognier likely to offer apricot, white peach and citrus blossom, with a touch of pear and subtle honeysuckle. On the palate it should be medium-bodied and supple rather than opulent, with enough freshness to keep the ripe fruit in check and a gently textured, dry finish.

wines.notes: Warwick’s The First Lady range is typically positioned as an accessible, restaurant-friendly bottling rather than a premium cuvée. Unoaked Chardonnay from the Cape usually sits in a modest retail bracket, with a Michelin-listing multiple applied for a practical by-the-glass or bottle-list estimate. Not live-verified bottle-by-bottle.
wines.tasting_note: A clean, unoaked Chardonnay in a bright, modern Cape style, likely to open with lemon zest, green apple, white peach and a touch of pear, with subtle almond and wet stone nuances. The palate should be medium-bodied and brisk, with crisp acidity, a supple, fruit-led core and a dry, refreshing finish rather than overt richness or oak-derived weight.

wines.notes: Likely a Sonoma-style Zinfandel of solid retail quality: ripe fruit, spice, and moderate structure. Priced as a practical estimate rather than a live market quote; Michelin-star list pricing reflects a standard restaurant markup for a mid-premium bottle.
wines.tasting_note: A serious East Bench Zinfandel from 2018 is likely to show ripe blackberry, black cherry and plum, with notes of cracked pepper, dried herbs and a touch of sweet spice. Expect a medium-full, supple palate with moderate tannin, bright acidity for the style, and a savoury, gently warming finish rather than overt sweetness or jamminess.
